findings.title: Interpolating before range-variable guard defeats no-split rule
findings.body: In querySplitting.ts runSplitQuery now does .filter(expr).map(applyTemplateVariables) and then partitions with querySupportsSplitting which checks !isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr). Because applyTemplateVariables expands template variables via replace (as the new test shows for $__auto/$step), an expr containing $__range/$__range_s/$__range_ms no longer contains that marker after interpolation. The guard therefore never fires and range-variable queries that must not be split are split. All split sub-requests then reuse the full-range interpolated value instead of each split range getting its own $__range, returning incorrect data.

findings.title: Filter-before-interpolate lets empty-after-interpolation queries through
findings.body: In shardQuerySplitting.ts runShardSplitQuery changed from interpolateVariablesInQueries(...).filter(expr).filter(!hide) to request.targets.filter(expr).filter(!hide).map(applyTemplateVariables). If a variable expands to empty (e.g. expr '$var' with empty value) the old code dropped the query after interpolation, the new code keeps it because emptiness is tested on the raw expr. That causes needless fetchLabelValues for __stream_shard__ with a bad selector and downstream shard sub-queries with empty selectors.

findings.title: Empty check runs on raw expr instead of interpolated expr
findings.body: In querySplitting.ts runSplitQuery filters !hide and query.expr before calling datasource.applyTemplateVariables. A query like expr '$expr' is non-empty before interpolation but can become '' after interpolation. Because the empty filter already ran, the query is kept, grouped, split and sent to runQuery instead of being ignored like other empty queries. This wastes requests and can send invalid empty selectors to the backend.
